title: New Zealand women waited 26 years to stand for Parliament
body: New Zealand women won the right to vote in parliamentary elections in 1893. The Women's Parliamentary Rights Act became law on 29 October 1919, allowing them to stand for the House of Representatives.
takeaway: Casting a vote and running for a seat are separate rights, and reforms can grant them decades apart.
source: New Zealand Parliament, Women's Parliamentary Rights centenary (2019)
visual: an empty candidate's chair beneath a tall window in an early twentieth-century parliamentary chamber

title: New Zealand gives each parliamentary voter two votes
body: After a referendum in 1993, New Zealand first used mixed-member proportional voting in its 1996 general election. One vote chooses a local representative. The other goes to a party and largely determines its share of seats.
takeaway: The two votes let someone choose a local candidate and support a different party nationally.
source: New Zealand Parliament, The 20th Anniversary of MMP (2016)
visual: a hand holding a folded blank ballot above a ballot box in a quiet polling station
